notes: §1985:VI.5.5.4 GR2 requires "The key word FILLER may be used to name a data item. Under no circumstances can a FILLER item be referred to explicitly", and allows that "the key word FILLER may be used to name a conditional variable". The grammar rule dataName admits the reserved word FILLER only as a data description entry's name, and CstExtensions.NameOrNull gives such an entry no name, so nothing can resolve to it; no identifier, qualifier, REDEFINES, RENAMES or DEPENDING ON position admits the word, and each explicit reference is refused at parse (COBOL5506 or COBOL0001; nine positions probed at --std 85). DataBinder.BindEntries associates a level-88 entry with the entry it follows whether or not that entry is named, so a FILLER item is a conditional variable for the condition test and for SET. The rule has no edition arm for a data description entry; the 1985 difference the change record names (FILLER in a report group description entry, a 2002 addition) is refused by VersionConformancePass.VisitReportGroupEntry. The witness declares elementary, group and level-01 FILLER items, tests and SETs condition-names on four of them, and displays the record; a probe added a group and a level-01 FILLER with members, an entry with the name omitted, and the refusals.

Under no circumstances can a FILLER item be referred to explicitly'; FILLER may name a conditional variable. §2023:13.18.20.4 GR1: 'The word FILLER may be used to name a data, report, or screen item.
